holidays.name: Random Acts of Kindness Day
holidays.description: A day for spreading unexpected niceness: paying for a stranger's coffee, leaving encouraging sticky notes, or holding the door a little too enthusiastically. It is observed in the U.S. and elsewhere, often as part of Random Acts of Kindness Week.
holidays.origin: Random Acts of Kindness Week was started by the Random Acts of Kindness Foundation, founded in 1995. The Foundation grew out of the 'practice random kindness and senseless acts of beauty' idea. February 17 is widely observed as the day itself, with the week built around it.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'random acts of kindness and senseless acts of beauty' was reportedly written by Anne Herbert on a placemat in a Sausalito, California restaurant in the 1980s, and it spread by bumper sticker.

holidays.name: Café au Lait Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the creamy, comforting French coffee drink made from equal parts strong coffee and steamed milk. Berets and dramatic sighing are optional but encouraged.
holidays.origin: Café au lait has been a French breakfast staple for centuries, with European versions dating back to at least the 1600s. The day is an unofficial food-calendar observance that gives coffee lovers a reason to sip something fancy-sounding.
holidays.funFact: In France, café au lait is traditionally a home breakfast drink, often served in a wide bowl so you can dunk your bread or croissant straight into it.

holidays.name: Set a Good Example Day
holidays.description: A day for realizing that someone is always watching you, whether it's a kid, a coworker, or the neighbor's dog. The idea is to behave like the best version of yourself, at least until dinner.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance in the modern holiday calendar, built around the old saying that actions speak louder than words. It is often attributed to the idea that character is shown by what you do when you think no one is looking.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists studying social learning, such as Albert Bandura with his 1961 Bobo doll experiments, showed that children copy adult behavior quite closely, which makes setting a good example more than just a catchy slogan.
